regulation: UK conformity assessment regime (UKCA / continued CE recognition)
article_ref: Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/696); sector regulations (Toys (Safety) Regs 2011, Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regs 2016)
title: United Kingdom: UKCA or CE marking for regulated product categories
summary: A product in a regulated category placed on the GB market must carry either UKCA or CE marking, supported by a conformity assessment and a declaration of conformity. GB continues to recognise CE marking for most categories; which applies depends on the sector. Flagged in v1; category depth is v2.

sources.title: The Product Safety and Metrology etc. (Amendment) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/696)
sources.note: Fetched directly, resolving the 13 Sept draft's unverified statutory reference. This SI (in force 1 Oct. 2024) is what actually makes the draft's central claim ('GB continues to recognise CE marking... indefinitely') current law: it revokes the sunset date that would otherwise have ended CE recognition, replacing it with open-ended recognition for the categories this row covers (toys, electrical equipment) among others. Confirms there is no fixed CE-recognition deadline as of this pass -- an earlier version of GB policy did have one (repeatedly extended before being made indefinite), so this is a live area to re-check periodically, not a one-time fact. Separately, note the UKCA marking itself may be affixed to a label/document rather than the product until 31 Dec 2027 (a labelling-location transitional rule, not a marking-choice one) -- not modelled in applies_when since it doesn't change which marking applies, only where it may be physically placed.

sources.title: Placing UKCA or CE marked products on the market in Great Britain — GOV.UK
sources.note: Re-fetched. Confirms toys and electrical equipment may use either CE or UKCA marking on the GB market, consistent with this row's applies_when covering both product.is_toy and product.is_electrical.
